finding: For the frozen nonlinear fixture, retaining exact theta while looking up C and K nearly eliminates the solver-response discrepancy. Retaining exact C alone or exact K alone does not.
design_implication: Prefer an asymmetric hydraulic representation over a uniformly tightened joint table: retention should be exact or independently near-exact, while C and K may use a looser frozen lookup subject to broader qualification.
next_gate: Measure the optimized cost of exact-theta plus lookup-C/K against full analytical evaluation and full lookup before implementing an end-to-end fast provider.
nonclaims: The result is not yet generalized across materials, boundary regimes or full SWAP trajectories.
The current Stage-A split provider is intentionally not performance optimized because it first evaluates the analytical provider.
